— Cybersecurity

Strengthen the foundations your business relies on.

A business website depends on more than its public pages. I help review the accounts, configuration, maintenance, and recovery steps that protect your online presence and the people who use it.

Discuss cybersecurity

A connected approach to cybersecurity

For many smaller businesses, meaningful security work starts with ordinary operational controls. The domain account needs strong protection, old administrator access needs review, and backups need a tested recovery path. A website can have a valid HTTPS certificate while still depending on an outdated plugin or an unmanaged form integration. Looking at these connections helps identify practical risks without overstating what a single assessment can prove.

When this work can help

  • No one has a clear inventory of website accounts and administrators.
  • Updates and backups happen inconsistently or have never been verified.
  • A growing set of plugins, forms, and integrations has unclear ownership.

How I approach the work

I agree the authorized systems, scope, access, and assessment boundaries before reviewing anything. The work can include configuration checks, access practices, maintenance records, and defensive website controls. Findings are explained in business terms and prioritized by likely impact and remediation effort. Any specialist testing, incident response, or regulated requirement needs an explicitly agreed scope and suitable expertise.

Core activities & deliverables

Access and ownership

Review domain, hosting, website, and connected-service access. Recommend named accounts, least privilege, strong authentication, and a process for removing access when responsibilities change.

Website protection

Review supported software, update practices, secure configuration, HTTPS, headers, forms, and exposed information. Reduce unnecessary components where that is a supported and approved change.

Resilience and guidance

Check backup coverage, retention, and restoration responsibilities. Document practical response steps and awareness guidance so the business knows who can act when something goes wrong.

Who this is for

This service suits small and medium-sized businesses seeking a practical review of their website and supporting accounts. It can accompany a new site, a maintenance plan, or a review of an existing provider arrangement. The business must own or have permission to assess the systems in scope. Access details and sensitive findings should be handled through an agreed secure channel.

What to consider before starting

A review cannot guarantee protection or identify every vulnerability. Security changes over time as software, integrations, and threats change. This service should not be presented as a certification, a compliance audit, a penetration test, or emergency incident response unless separately scoped and supported. Active compromise or highly regulated requirements may require a dedicated specialist.

How we assess progress

Useful outcomes include a clear inventory, accountable ownership, reduced unnecessary access, supported software, and a verified recovery procedure. Recommendations should include what was checked, what remains outside scope, and how remediation can be confirmed. A list of tool findings alone is not evidence that the business is protected.

Questions about cybersecurity

Does an assessment guarantee my site is secure?+

No. It identifies issues within an agreed scope at a point in time. Ongoing maintenance, access management, monitoring, and incident preparation remain necessary.

Can you assess a system I do not own?+

Only systems for which you have clear authorization can be included. The scope and permission must be established before any review.
